1.title: IP Network Services: DHCP, DNS and Time
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: I P Network Services: D H C P, D N S and Time. It covers the exam area three point zero Network Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. three point four Given a scenario, implement IPv four and IPv six network services: dynamic addressing (D H C P reservations, scope, lease time, options, relay and I P helper, exclusions. S L A A C). Name resolution (D N S, D N S S E C, Do H and Do T, record types, zone types, authoritative versus non-authoritative, primary versus secondary, recursive, hosts file). Time protocols (N T P, P T P, N T S). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three point zero Network Operations (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: DHCP
1.text: D H C P. Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (D H C P) assigns I P configuration automatically. The four steps are D O R A: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

1.title: DHCP, continued
1.text: D H C P. The figure shows this: The D H C P D O R A exchange: discover, offer, request, acknowledge.

1.title: DHCP, continued
1.text: D H C P. Scope. The range of addresses the server can lease. Exclusions. Addresses inside the scope that are never leased (for static devices). Reservation. Always gives the same address to a specific M A C address. Lease time. How long a client keeps an address before renewing. Options. Extra settings sent to clients: default gateway, D N S servers, domain name. Relay or I P helper. A router forwards D H C P broadcasts to a server on another subnet. S L A A C (stateless address autoconfiguration, IPv six). A host builds its own IPv six address from the router's prefix without a D H C P server. Exam tip: "D H C P server is on another subnet" equals configure a relay (I P helper) on the router. "A printer must always keep the same I P" equals a reservation.

1.title: DNS
1.text: D N S. Domain Name System (D N S) resolves names to I P addresses (port fifty-three). A. Name to IPv four address. A A A A. Name to IPv six address. C N A M E. Alias to another name. M X. Mail servers for the domain. T X T. Text, verification, S P F or dee kim. N S. Authoritative name servers for the zone. P T R. I P address to name (reverse lookup).

1.title: DNS, continued
1.text: D N S. Forward zone or reverse zone. Name to address or address to name. Authoritative. Holds the zone's records (the source of truth); non-authoritative answers come from a cache. Primary or secondary. Primary holds the writable zone; secondary keeps a read-only copy by zone transfer. Recursive resolver. Does the full lookup on the client's behalf, asking other servers. D N S S E C. Digitally signs records to prove they are authentic (protects integrity, not privacy). Do H or Do T. D N S over H T T P S (port four hundred forty-three) or D N S over T L S (port eight hundred fifty-three): encrypt D N S queries for privacy. Hosts file. A local file of name-to-address mappings, checked before D N S. Exam tip: D N S S E C proves authenticity; Do H and Do T hide the query. M X equals mail; P T R equals reverse lookup; C N A M E equals alias.

1.title: Time protocols
1.text: Time protocols. N T P (Network Time Protocol). Synchronizes clocks, U D P one hundred twenty-three, hierarchy of strata; accurate time matters for logs, certificates and authentication. P T P (Precision Time Protocol). Sub-microsecond accuracy for industrial and financial networks. N T S (Network Time Security). Adds authentication and encryption to N T P. Exam tip: D H C P relay equals I P helper on the router; reservation equals fixed address for a M A C; exclusion equals never leased.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Clients in a branch subnet cannot get addresses from the central D H C P server. What should be configured on the branch router? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A D H C P relay (I P helper). A relay forwards D H C P broadcasts across subnets.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A network printer must always receive the same address from D H C P. What should be created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A D H C P reservation. A reservation binds an address to a M A C address.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which D N S record maps a hostname to an IPv six address? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A A A A. A A A A records hold IPv six addresses.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which D N S feature proves that a response was not tampered with? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: D N S S E C. D N S S E C signs records to prove authenticity.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company wants D N S queries hidden from observers on the network. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: D N S over H T T P S. Do H encrypts D N S queries.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which protocol keeps device clocks synchronized for accurate log timestamps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: N T P. N T P synchronizes time on U D P one hundred twenty-three.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does D O R A stand for? Answer: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge. Question two. What does a P T R record do? Answer: Maps an I P address to a name. Question three. What does S L A A C do? Answer: Lets an IPv six host build its own address from the router's prefix.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which port does N T P use? Answer: U D P one hundred twenty-three. Question five. What is a D H C P exclusion? Answer: Addresses in the scope that are never leased. Question six. What does a recursive resolver do? Answer: Performs the full lookup on the client's behalf.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. D H C P: D O R A; scope, exclusions, reservation, lease, options, relay; S L A A C for IPv six. D N S records: A, A A A A, C N A M E, M X, T X T, N S, P T R. D N S concepts: forward and reverse, authoritative, primary and secondary, recursive, D N S S E C, Do H or Do T, hosts file. Time: N T P (U D P one hundred twenty-three), P T P (precise), N T S (secure).
